title: Metadata Pre-Filtering
summary: Restrict the searchable evidence set using trusted metadata before semantic ranking, while validating the store’s actual filtering behavior.
overview: Metadata pre-filtering narrows candidate documents by tenant, access rights, language, time, or business scope before or within nearest-neighbor search. It improves relevance and can enforce an important retrieval boundary, but its security depends on the provenance and enforcement of the filter. A model-generated tenant identifier is not an authorization decision.

Vector stores differ in how filtering interacts with approximate indexes. Some apply scalar filters first; others combine filtering with iterative search or specialized indexes. Very selective predicates can affect latency and recall. Architects must evaluate their chosen implementation and recheck access when fetching the underlying text.

production.poc: A prototype adds explicit tenant and document-type metadata and tests retrieval with intentionally similar cross-tenant content.
production.production: Production derives filters from authenticated identity, validates metadata at ingestion, and tests permission revocation.
production.scale: Enterprise scale requires group-expansion strategies, high-cardinality filter indexes, selective-query benchmarks, and consistent authorization across search, cache, and source fetch.

components.name: Identity resolver
components.role: Obtains trusted tenant and group membership from the application security context.

components.name: Policy compiler
components.role: Builds an allowed metadata predicate independent of model suggestions.

components.name: Metadata catalog
components.role: Stores validated ownership, classification, validity, and document-version fields.

components.name: Filtered search engine
components.role: Combines the trusted predicate with vector retrieval.

components.name: Source fetch gate
components.role: Revalidates access before exposing the matched document body.

flow.title: Authenticate the request
flow.description: Resolve principal identity and the relevant policy revision.

flow.title: Compile allowed scope
flow.description: Construct a mandatory filter and combine optional user preferences without weakening it.

flow.title: Validate predicate
flow.description: Reject missing ownership fields, unsupported operators, or excessively broad expansions.

flow.title: Execute filtered retrieval
flow.description: Run vector search using the store’s supported filtering mode and bounded candidate parameters.

flow.title: Recheck source access
flow.description: Authorize the final document fetch against current access state.

flow.title: Record evidence scope
flow.description: Retain policy and source revisions for investigation without logging sensitive document content.

useCase.title: Searching client matter documents
useCase.situation: A law firm assistant searches documents across many client matters with overlapping terminology.
useCase.problem: Semantic similarity alone retrieves highly relevant documents belonging to another client.
useCase.requirement: Retrieve only evidence allowed for the current lawyer and matter.
useCase.architecture: A policy compiler resolves matter permissions and passes immutable scope to search and document fetch.
runtime: The lawyer asks about a clause within a selected matter.
The service applies the permitted matter set before retrieval and rechecks each final document.
useCase.failure: If a document’s access changes after indexing, source fetch denies it and the answer proceeds with remaining authorized evidence or reports insufficient coverage.
useCase.impact: Measure denied-fetch events, revocation lag, and selective-filter recall; an empty authorized result is preferable to a plausible unauthorized answer.

tradeoffs.cost: Selective predicates may stress approximate-search behavior.
Increases ingestion validation and index maintenance.

failures.detection: New records appear outside expected partitions.
failures.recovery: Reject or quarantine records lacking mandatory ownership fields.

failures.detection: A removed user still matches cached access filters.
failures.recovery: Expire policy caches and invalidate affected retrieval sessions.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the model choose tenant scope
mistakes.fix: Derive mandatory scope from authenticated context.
Use supported constrained search and measure recall under selective predicates.

mistakes.mistake: Assuming index ACLs are always current
mistakes.fix: Reauthorize final source access and monitor update lag.

whenToUse: Use for multi-tenant or access-controlled retrieval.
Use when documents have meaningful time or business partitions.
Use to constrain searches to an explicit task scope.
whenNotToUse: Do not trust unvalidated ingestion metadata.
Avoid treating similarity thresholds as access controls.
Do not add arbitrary filters without understanding their recall cost.
